scope.purpose: Pre-architecture threat model for an AI support assistant that summarizes enterprise documents and drafts or possibly executes account changes
scope.environment: Fictional idea; architecture, implementation, execution authority, deployment, and cloud provider undecided

exclusions.reason: No repository, architecture, or deployment exists.
No target exists and testing was not authorized.

scope.risk_policy: Not supplied; priorities are provisional, not release decisions.

sources.description: Fictional early feature idea for document summarization and account-change recommendations or execution.

assets.description: Sensitive enterprise customer documents and derived summaries
assets.harm: Cross-tenant disclosure, confidentiality breach, unintended retention, or secondary use.

assets.description: Enterprise account configuration, integrity, and privileged change capability
assets.harm: Unauthorized or harmful changes, outage, financial loss, or loss of trust.

assets.description: Integrity and provenance of summaries, recommendations, approvals, and audit records
assets.harm: Misleading support action, repudiation, unsafe automation, or inability to investigate.

actors.description: Authorized support operator using the assistant
capabilities: Potentially approve changes if product permits

actors.description: Enterprise customer user or attacker able to influence an uploaded document
capabilities: Place arbitrary instructions and sensitive content in documents
Attempt to influence downstream assistant behavior
Request excessive summaries or account changes

components.description: Provisional document upload/intake and tenant-context surface
Assumed logical document/derived-data storage; technology and retention undecided
Provisional AI assistant/orchestration component for summarization and recommendations
Conditional account-change interface; may be suggestion-only or executable
Provisional support review, approval, and audit surface

boundaries.description: Trust boundary between untrusted uploaded content and assistant instructions/context
Enterprise tenant and support-operator authorization boundary around documents and accounts
Privilege boundary between generated recommendation and any account-changing action

flows.data: Untrusted, potentially sensitive enterprise document and tenant metadata
Document content and tenant-scoped context for summarization
Summary, recommended changes, provenance, and uncertainty
Conditional account-change request and authorization context

invariants.statement: Uploaded content is always treated as untrusted data and cannot alter governing instructions, select tools, expand authority, or bypass approval.
Documents, derived data, model context, outputs, and account actions remain bound to the correct tenant and authorized support case.
No account change occurs without explicit permitted action, current authorization, bounded parameters, independent policy validation, and an attributable approval/audit record.
Sensitive content is minimized, protected, purpose-limited, retained/deleted by approved policy, and not exposed to unapproved model providers or training.
Summaries and recommendations expose source provenance and uncertainty and are not treated as authoritative account state.

evidence.observation: Idea proposes a support assistant to summarize untrusted, potentially sensitive enterprise documents and draft account changes; whether it may execute changes is explicitly undecided; no repository, architecture, or cloud access exists.

assumptions.statement: The assistant might receive authority to execute account changes rather than only draft them.
assumptions.verification_plan: Choose suggestion-only or execution mode; if execution is retained, define the exact allowlisted actions, parameters, approvals, and rollback.

assumptions.statement: Model/provider, data-use terms, retention, isolation, and tool architecture are undecided.
assumptions.verification_plan: Select architecture/provider and document data flows, contracts, training use, retention, residency, logging, and subprocessors.

assumptions.statement: Tenant identity, support-case scope, operator permissions, and approval policy can be established independently of document content.
assumptions.verification_plan: Define principal-action-resource-context tuple and test tenant/case/action enforcement.

threats.title: Indirect prompt injection drives unsafe recommendations or actions
prerequisites: Document text can influence orchestration, tool calls, hidden context, or operator decisions
attack_steps: Embed instructions in an uploaded document
Assistant interprets content as governing instruction or persuasive action
Assistant leaks context, proposes a deceptive change, or invokes privileged behavior
threats.harm: Unauthorized change, sensitive-data disclosure, or support operator deception.

risk.rationale: Untrusted documents and possible account-change authority are explicit; architecture is unknown. If execution is prohibited, impact reduces but deceptive recommendations remain.
risk.residual_risk: Model behavior is probabilistic; content controls cannot alone establish safe authorization.

threats.next_action: Default to suggestion-only and design strict instruction/data separation plus independent authorization before deciding whether execution is allowed.

threats.title: Cross-tenant document, context, or output disclosure
prerequisites: Tenant/case context is client-controlled, stale, shared, cached, or missing at any read/write/model boundary
attack_steps: Select or guess another tenant's document, conversation, cache entry, or account
Trigger retrieval, summarization, or action with incorrect context
Receive information or affect the other tenant
threats.harm: Enterprise confidentiality breach or unauthorized account impact.

risk.rationale: Enterprise documents are sensitive; all isolation mechanisms are undecided.
risk.residual_risk: Shared provider infrastructure and operational access remain until contracts, architecture, and tests bound them.

threats.next_action: Define tenant/case binding across upload, storage, retrieval, model context, logs, cache, output, and action.

threats.title: Overprivileged or insufficiently approved account changes
prerequisites: Assistant/tool credentials or approval paths permit broad, stale, or ambiguous authority
attack_steps: Generate or manipulate a proposed account change
Bypass, confuse, or over-broaden approval and parameter validation
Execute a harmful or wrong-tenant change
threats.harm: Account compromise, outage, financial or contractual harm, and weak accountability.

risk.rationale: Execution authority is undecided; granting it creates a direct privileged path with potentially irreversible harm.
risk.residual_risk: Even approved changes can be mistaken; rollback, separation of duties, and explicit risk acceptance may be required per action class.

threats.next_action: Keep suggestion-only unless an owner approves narrowly allowlisted actions and a reviewed authorization/approval design.

threats.title: Sensitive document data is over-collected, retained, logged, trained on, or sent to an unapproved provider
prerequisites: Data lifecycle and provider terms do not constrain collection, context, logs, retention, training, residency, or subprocessors
attack_steps: System propagates excessive content into storage, prompts, telemetry, provider systems, or training
Data persists or is accessed beyond customer purpose and expectation
threats.harm: Privacy/confidentiality breach and contractual or regulatory exposure.

risk.rationale: Sensitive content is explicit while every lifecycle/provider choice is absent.
risk.residual_risk: Authorized processing still exposes content to approved operators/providers; customer terms and incident obligations require owner approval.

threats.next_action: Approve data classification, minimization, provider, retention/deletion, training-use, residency, and logging rules.

threats.title: Hallucinated or incomplete summary causes a harmful support decision
prerequisites: Output lacks source grounding, uncertainty, completeness checks, or human review appropriate to impact
attack_steps: Assistant omits or invents material facts
Operator approves or performs an inappropriate account change
threats.harm: Incorrect account state, customer harm, delay, and unreliable audit trail.

risk.rationale: Summarization and recommendations are explicit uses; accuracy thresholds and human workflow are absent.
risk.residual_risk: Grounded outputs can still be incomplete or misunderstood; high-impact decisions need human accountability.

threats.next_action: Define source-citation, uncertainty, review, action-class, and evaluation requirements.

controls.requirement: Keep uploaded text in a typed untrusted-data channel; do not let it select tools, reveal hidden context, alter policy, or supply authorization; constrain model output to validated schemas and treat it as untrusted.
Bind tenant and support-case context server-side across upload, storage, retrieval, cache/memory, prompt assembly, outputs, logs, and actions; authorize every access against current operator scope.

Default to suggestion-only. If execution is approved, expose only allowlisted typed actions with least-privilege short-lived credentials, independent current authorization and policy validation, explicit human confirmation showing exact tenant/change, idempotency, audit, rollback, and step-up/separation for high impact.

Minimize and classify content; approve provider/region/subprocessors and no-training terms; redact where possible; protect storage/transit; exclude sensitive content from logs; enforce tenant-specific retention, deletion, and legal-hold rules.

Ground summaries and recommendations in visible source citations, distinguish facts from inference, expose uncertainty/coverage, require impact-appropriate human review, and evaluate material omission and fabrication before release.

checks.procedure: In an authorized test environment, evaluate a versioned multilingual/obfuscated indirect-prompt-injection corpus across summarization, recommendation, hidden-context exfiltration, and tool-selection paths.
checks.expected: Document content cannot alter policy, reveal hidden/other-tenant context, select tools, or cause action; outputs remain schema-valid and visibly untrusted.
checks.reason: No implementation or test target exists.

checks.procedure: Attempt cross-tenant/case access through identifiers, retrieval, cache, conversations, logs, model context, outputs, and actions, including permission revocation.
checks.expected: Every path denies with no data, derived output, side channel, or action; revocation meets the approved bound.
checks.reason: No implementation or test target exists.

checks.procedure: Verify suggestion-only mode has no execution credential/path; if execution is approved, abuse-test action allowlists, parameter validation, tenant binding, stale/replayed approvals, privilege, idempotency, audit, and rollback.
checks.expected: No unapproved action occurs; exact approved action/tenant/parameters are enforced and attributable; forbidden/high-impact cases fail safely.
checks.reason: Execution authority and implementation are undecided.

checks.procedure: Inspect end-to-end data flow and provider contracts/configuration; test retention/deletion, logging/redaction, access, residency, and training-use controls with synthetic data.
checks.expected: Only approved minimal data reaches approved locations; no sensitive logs/training; access, retention, deletion, and contractual terms match policy.
checks.reason: No architecture, provider, implementation, or policy exists.

checks.procedure: Evaluate a representative, adversarial, versioned document set for citation support, material omissions, contradictions, fabricated facts, uncertainty calibration, and operator overreliance.
checks.expected: Owner-approved quality thresholds are met; every material claim is traceable; unsupported claims and insufficient coverage are clearly surfaced.
checks.reason: No model, dataset, thresholds, workflow, or test target exists.

Reviewed malicious documents influencing support outcomes.
File processing, malware handling, quotas, observability, and incident design are unavailable.

Reviewed tenant/case authorization and action scope.
Reviewed cross-tenant disclosure and data lifecycle.
Reviewed compromised support identity and wrong-tenant action.
Identity, cache, support operations, audit, and incident processes are undecided.
Reviewed tenant isolation across model context, memory, and outputs.
Reviewed least privilege, approval, validation, and rollback.
Reviewed disclosure through recommendations/actions and audit data.
Reviewed operator overreliance and privileged misuse.
Action catalog, approvals, rollback, monitoring, and incident response are undecided.
